etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French carnation (“person's color or complexion”).

definitions.definition: other members of genus Dianthus and hybrids
(botany) A type of Eurasian plant widely cultivated for its flowers.
The type of flower they bear, originally flesh-coloured, but since hybridizing found in a variety of colours.

quote.text: And the women of New Bedford, they bloom like their own red roses. But roses only bloom in summer; whereas the fine carnation of their cheeks is perennial as sunlight in the seventh heavens.

definitions.definition: (archaic) The pinkish colors used in art to render human face and flesh
Of a rosy pink or red colour.
